newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - Tues, Dec 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - Tues, Dec 17.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- MISSING LEVITT FACES ARREST ON DIRECTOR BAN

A London magistrate court has issued a warrant to arrest Roger Levitt, the former investment manager, after he failed to appear in court on a charge of breaking a ban on acting as a director. The Department of Trade said Levitt took on a high profile directorship at the International Boxing Corp days after he was barred from holding a director position for seven years.
-- HOUSE PRICES 'WILL RISE 46 PERCENT IN FOUR YEARS'

Rob Thomas of stockbroker UBS says house prices will rise by an average of 10 percent next year and a total of 46 percent by the end of the year 2000. He says low inflation and low interest rates could combine to push up house prices. Economists at both the largest lenders, Halifax Building Society and Abbey National, have distanced themselves from this prediction.
-- HOLLINGER SELLS FAIRFAX STAKE
Hollinger International is to sell out of John Fairfax five years after it first agreed the financing package with the receivers to the publisher of Australia's leading newspapers.

The stake is being sold to Brierley Investments of New Zealand for 553.8 million Australian dollars. Hollinger is to sell after its ambition to raise its stake was thwarted by the Australian government's refusal to change media ownership rules.
THE TIMES
-- FT-SE BLOW TO HALIFAX SHAREHOLDERS

If a proposal to delay the entry of Halifax Building Society into the Stock Exchange indices goes ahead, millions of members could see the value of their shares drop after conversion next June. Halifax would normally qualify for fast entry to the FT-SE 100 index because of its estimated market value of 10 billion stg, which is equivalent to more than one percent of market value of the index. But the Halifax conversion will offer shares only to its nine million members and the FT-SE Actuaries UK Indices Committee believes the lack of an institutional placing could distort the market and is considering a three-week delay.
-- BASS IN 400 MILLION STG INNS DEAL

The brewing and leisure group Bass is selling 47 American Holiday Inn hotels to Bristol Hotels Group of the U.S. in a 400-million-stg deal as part of its strategy to franchise hotels rather than own them outright. Bass will take shareholding of 36.1 percent in Bristol, which will become the largest hotel operator in America. Bass will also sell management contracts for another 14 hotels to Bristol, receive 91 million dollars in cash and retire 300 million dollars in debt.
-- RBS EXECUTIVE NETS TWO MILLION STG BONUS

Lawrence Fish, chairman of the Citizens Financial Group, the Royal Bank of Scotland's U.S. subsidiary, has netted two million stg in bonuses since its merger with First NH Bank in April. The bonus to Fish doubled the amount of bonuses paid to eight executive directors to 2.4 million stg in 1996. RBS said the bonus was in line with comparable executives in America and was well deserved because Citizens' profits had risen by 57 percent.
THE GUARDIAN
-- SELLAFIELD STORM OVER PLAN TO INCREASE DISCHARGES

British Nuclear Fuel's 2.3 billion stg Thorp thermal oxide reprocessing plant at Sellafield is to be hit by delays by a row over plans for an increase in discharges from the plant. Nearly three years after it began operations, the plant still has not been commissioned by government safety officials. The company has applied to change the radioactive discharges from the plant and faces legal hurdles in justifying them to the Environment Agency and the public.
-- CABLE FIRMS ANGERED BY OFT RULING ON MURDOCH

Following the Office of Fair Trading's decision to approve a revised rate card for the supply of BSkyB channels to cable operators, the Cable Communications Association is considering an appeal to the European Commission or a High Court judicial review because they believe this to be unfair. It said it disagreed with the conclusion that there were no adverse effects from the rate card. BSkyB's revised rate card gives cable operators the option to choose discount structures.
-- TOP INSURANCE BROKERS MERGE

Prompted by the increasing competitive market environment, Lloyd Thompson Group and JIB Group, two of Britain's leading insurance brokers, are to merge in a 300 million stg deal. This will form London's third largest brokerage firm. Chief executive of Lloyd Thompson, Ken Carter, will run the enlarged company and said the main attraction of the deal was the complementary nature of the two companies' operations.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- AIRBUS SHRUGS OFF JET MERGER THREAT

The European aircraft manufacturer Airbus Industrie has conceded that the Boeing takeover of McDonnell Douglas had increased the urgency for it to push ahead with its own reconstructuring into a fully commercial organisation. Airbus Industrie, a four-nation consortium, also shrugged off suggestions that the merger of its two U.S. rivals would undermine it position in the civil jet market.
-- OECD PRAISES UK ECONOMIC POLICIES

According to the end-of-year report of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, government economic policies have delivered the best growth and inflation prospects in 30 years. The report says strong growth, falling unemployment and low inflation are signs of the positive benefits of past and ongoing macroeconomic policy framework. But it said progress in reducing the government's budget deficit has been too slow.
-- PRISM FOUNDERS GET SHARES WORTH 5.4 MILLION STG

Seven founding members of the company set up to tender for passenger train franchises, Prism Rail, have been awarded free shares worth 5.4 million stg. The owners already own more than a third of Prism's shares, worth over 30 million stg. This came after announcing plans to finance their fourth successful bid, a 12 million stg rights issue to help fund the contract to operate West Anglia Great Northern railway.
